_note: innoferra 10-01: plain-language metadata for every real-traffic replay in runs_v3.json (numbers come from runs_v3.json, produced on node 0008 by serving/minimax-m3.1/extract_runs.py). at = PDT time the run finished. protocol v3 = before Oct 1 04:30 PDT (replayed the requests production rejected with 429 + media-tag bug); v3.1 = current.

runs.name: Starting setup (old routing: sessions pinned by arrival)
runs.why: Traffic piled onto 2 of the 4 engines while the other 2 sat idle.

runs.name: Production-style numerics (FP8 KV cache, training-compatible mode off)
runs.why: FP8 cache holds half as many tokens, so cache hits fell to 83.5% and prompts had to be reprocessed. Quality was fine (GSM8K 96.7%).

runs.name: Dynamo KV-aware router (production's router), default affinity
runs.why: Load spread evenly but cache reuse collapsed to 65% (ours 94%): each engine has two separate caches and Dynamo did not pin the right one.

runs.name: Dynamo KV-aware router, strong affinity
runs.why: Cache reuse only recovered to 71%.

runs.name: Load-aware routing (new sessions to the least-busy engine, move overloaded sessions)
runs.why: Routing balanced all 4 engines, which exposed the real limit: every engine queued requests and decode fell to 38 tok/s.

runs.name: Load-aware routing
runs.why: Routing fixed the pile-up (2/15 → 7/15). Misses came from huge cold prompts and from 6 errors caused by a media-tag bug (fixed later).

runs.name: Load-aware routing
runs.why: Median TTFT just above 1 s and decode 53 tok/s: prompt processing pauses token generation on both GPUs of an engine.

runs.name: + more GPU memory for the cache (0.68 → 0.76)
runs.why: Fewer evicted sessions: median TTFT 1.19 → 1.01 s, 42% fewer first tokens over 10 s. Decode still below 60.

runs.name: + fair-share prefill (waiting requests get half of each prefill step)
runs.why: An engine ran out of cache memory mid-prefill and crashed. Root cause patched; the test is queued again.

runs.name: Load-aware routing (re-run on the current test)
runs.why: Same settings as 03:56 on the corrected test: 7/15 → 9/15. The 6 misses are slow-tail TTFT from 300k+-token prompts and one median miss.

runs.name: + shorter speculative-decoding blocks (DSpark block 7 → 4)
runs.why: The draft model's acceptance fell 3.66 → 3.06 tokens per step, so decode dropped 55 → 46 tok/s.

runs.name: + smaller prompt-processing chunks (32k → 16k)
runs.why: Slightly worse on TTFT and decode: smaller chunks add steps without cutting total prefill time.

runs.name: Adopted settings (load-aware routing + 0.76 cache memory)
runs.why: 13/15: both misses are median TTFT 1.02 and 1.05 s. Slow tail and decode beat production on the same requests.

runs.name: Adopted settings (load-aware routing + 0.76 cache memory)
runs.why: 10/15 (9/15 with the old memory setting): slow-tail TTFT improved 14.3 → 11.7 s; misses are 3 median-TTFT minutes just over 1 s and 3 slow-tail minutes.

runs.name: + longest-cached-prompt-first scheduling (on top of 0.76 cache memory)
runs.why: Same 1/15, but every rule improved: slow-tail TTFT 18.3 → 13.4 s, decode 55 → 57 tok/s, fewer failing minutes on each rule. Decode below 60 is still the main miss at this load.

runs.name: + 128 running requests per engine (64 per GPU)
runs.why: Both GPUs' schedulers died while capturing the CUDA graphs for 64 running requests each; the engines crash-looped and the run never started.

runs.name: + fair-share prefill, retried with the out-of-memory fix (on top of capacity + longest-prefix-first)
runs.why: No crash this time (fix works), but worse: slow-tail TTFT 13.4 → 18.5 s, median 0.98 → 1.03 s, decode 57 → 55 tok/s.

runs.name: Adopted settings + longest-cached-prompt-first scheduling
runs.why: 13/15 again: the two misses moved (median first token 1.19 s in minute 1, 1.02 s in minute 10). Our per-minute medians swing 0.63–1.19 s around the 1 s line, so the first-token floor itself must come down.

runs.name: Adopted settings + longest-cached-prompt-first scheduling
runs.why: 9/15, but the slow tail is fixed (worst first token 9.5 s, 0 minutes over 15 s). All 6 misses are the median first token just over 1 s — the per-request tokenisation floor.

runs.name: + 8 tokenizer processes (adopted settings + cache-first)
runs.why: 10/15 vs 9/15 with 4 processes: median first token 0.94 → 0.90 s and median misses 6 → 3 minutes, but 2 slow-tail minutes came back. Within run-to-run noise.

runs.name: + 1 tokenizer process with a larger tokenisation cache
runs.why: 1/15: median first token 1.26 s (0.90–0.94 with 4–8 processes). One process also carries all HTTP and streaming work, which outweighs its cache hits.

runs.name: + 8 tokenizer processes (adopted settings + cache-first)
runs.why: 13/15 again: misses are minutes 0 and 1 (median first token 1.02 and 1.11 s). Across four 1.79 M runs the misses sit in the first two minutes and are 0.02–0.19 s over the limit.

runs.name: + parallel tokenising (16 pieces)
runs.why: Aborted after 8 of 15 minutes: slowest-1% first tokens 25–60 s per minute (6–15 s without) and decode 54–67 tok/s; the extra tokenizer threads most likely starve the GPU scheduler processes. Retesting with 4 pieces.

runs.name: + parallel tokenising (4 pieces)
runs.why: 5/15 vs 10/15 without it: slowest-1% first tokens 15–28 s in several minutes. Even 4 pieces hurt the engine, so parallel tokenising inside the tokenizer processes is dropped.

runs.name: + warm prompts step ahead of long uncached chunks
runs.why: 9/15 vs 10/15 without it: median first token over 1 s in 4 minutes (1.04–1.13 s), slowest-1% over 15 s in 2. Warm requests seldom wait behind uncached chunks, so the ~1 s median is not queueing.

runs.name: 8 tokenizer processes, repeat run (noise check)
runs.why: 11/15 on the settings that gave 10/15 earlier: identical runs differ by about one minute. Misses: median 1.10 and 1.05 s (minutes 0, 11); slowest-1% 16–24 s in minutes 11, 12, 14.

runs.name: + shared tokenisation cache across 8 processes
runs.why: 12/15 (same settings without it: 10 and 11). Every minute passes the median rule (worst 0.98 s); the 3 misses are slowest-1% only (21–24 s, huge uncached prompts). Kept as part of the tokenisation fix.

runs.name: + shared cache, no second tokenising pass
runs.why: 12/15 with median first token 0.54 s (0.85 with the shared cache alone; every minute 0.49–0.61 s) and overall p99 10.8 s (production 10.4). All 3 misses are the slowest-1% rule (16–22 s, huge uncached prompts).

runs.name: + one decode step after each prefill
runs.why: 15/15 under both the old strict rule and the new SLA; slowest 1% 8.2 s (production 10.4, without it 10.8) and every minute ≤ 14.5 s. Generation speed unchanged (76 vs 78 tok/s).

runs.name: production attention path, our 4-bit KV
runs.why: The engine refuses it: its fast 4-bit-KV path needs MiniMax's MSA kernel and does not allow speculative decoding. Stopped after 5 minutes; the 8-bit KV variant runs next.

runs.name: production numerics (attention + 8-bit KV)
runs.why: About 0/15 at 3.34 M: median first token 1.1–8.6 s and generation 45–66 tok/s per minute; 8-bit KV holds half the tokens, so prompts are re-processed (hit 91.2%). Replay tail cut 24 min after the window.

runs.name: decode after prefill at ¾ load (baseline)
runs.why: 2/15: median first token 0.53–0.85 s per minute, but generation 40–66 tok/s (51.5 overall vs production 64.8) fails 13 minutes. Baseline for the draft-graph and prefill-delayer runs.

runs.name: + draft model replays its CUDA graph
runs.why: 11/15 at 3.34 M (baseline 2/15): generation 64.1 tok/s per stream, production 64.8 on the same requests (+24%); acceptance unchanged 3.64, 0 errors. Minutes 9–12 still 50–55 tok/s.

runs.name: + pair the two GPUs' prompt pieces
runs.why: 15/15 at 3.34 M, the first pass at this load: generation 63–93 tok/s per minute (74.5 overall vs production 64.8), median first token 1.1–1.7 s, 0 errors, acceptance 3.66.

runs.name: A/A twin, group A
runs.why: Twin calibration (same settings on both 2-engine groups, same half of the sessions): 10/15, generation 61.4 tok/s, median first token 0.64 s. Paired B vs A: −0.3 tok/s (95% CI −1.5..+1.1).

runs.name: A/A twin, group B
runs.why: Twin calibration (same settings on both 2-engine groups, same half of the sessions): 10/15, generation 63.3 tok/s, median first token 0.61 s. Paired B vs A: −0.3 tok/s (95% CI −1.5..+1.1).

runs.name: full stack at full load
runs.why: 3/15 at 4.42 M: median first token 1.3–2.0 s and 0 errors, but generation 40–58 tok/s in minutes 3–13 (52.4 overall vs production 64.6). Old stack at this load: 0/15, 37.9 tok/s, first token 9.0 s.

runs.name: control half (adopted settings)
runs.why: Control half of the twin run: 15/15 at 3.34 M per GPU, generation 76.0 tok/s, median first token 1.43 s, 0 errors (re-confirms the 3.34 M pass on half the sessions).

runs.name: + production's host-overhead flags
runs.why: Paired against the control on the same requests: generation −2.15 tok/s (95% CI −3.7..−0.5), first token unchanged; 12/15. Plan stream, incremental streaming, local control broadcast and recv interval 2 bundled.

runs.name: control half at full load
runs.why: Control half at full load (4.42 M per GPU): 6/15, generation 58.3 tok/s, median first token 1.50 s, 0 errors.

runs.name: + three decode steps after each prefill
runs.why: Paired against the control on the same requests: generation +0.22 tok/s (95% CI −0.9..+1.7), first token −2% (CI −6..+1%); 6/15 both. One step stays.

runs.name: control half at full load
runs.why: Control half at full load (4.42 M per GPU): 8/15, generation 59.6 tok/s, median first token 1.47 s, 0 errors; uncached prompt 12.6 M tokens.

runs.name: + KV memory 0.80 (production's share)
runs.why: Paired against the control on the same requests: generation −0.99 tok/s (95% CI −1.9..+0.4), first token +3% (CI +0.4..+7%); 6/15. 15% more GPU and host cache (2.13 M GPU + 6.38 M host tokens per GPU, above production's 2.10 M + 6.31 M) left the cache hit unchanged at 95.4% and the uncached prompt at 12.2 M tokens: the remaining misses are not a capacity problem.

runs.name: control half at full load
runs.why: Control half at full load (4.42 M per GPU): 6/15, generation 58.6 tok/s, median first token 1.49 s, 0 errors; uncached prompt 12.4 M tokens.

runs.name: + write-back host cache
runs.why: Paired against the control on the same requests: generation +0.18 tok/s (95% CI −0.8..+1.3), first token +0.7% (CI −2..+4%); 7/15; uncached prompt 11.9 M vs 12.4 M. New drop counters show zero failed backups and zero dropped cache entries in BOTH groups: the host cache is full and evicts by plain LRU, so write-back has nothing to fix. Write-through stays (write-back has a known crash under load, sglang #19212).

runs.name: control half at full load
runs.why: Control half at full load (4.42 M per GPU): 7/15, generation 59.6 tok/s, median first token 1.53 s, 0 errors; uncached prompt 12.3 M tokens.

runs.name: + new sessions placed by in-flight context size
runs.why: Paired against the control on the same requests: generation −4.87 tok/s (95% CI −6.5..−3.4), first token +56% (CI +43..+68%), first-token p99 106 s; 6/15; uncached prompt 16.9 M vs 12.3 M. A GPU with little context in flight attracts every new (small) session until they grow, so sessions bunch up and the cache churns. Request-count placement stays.

runs.name: control half at full load
runs.why: Control half at full load (4.42 M per GPU): 6/15, generation 57.5 tok/s, median first token 1.57 s, 0 errors; uncached prompt 13.2 M tokens.

runs.name: + prompt chunks sized by cost
runs.why: Paired against the control on the same requests: generation +2.69 tok/s (95% CI +1.6..+3.8), median first token −8% (CI −11..−4%), first-token p99 13.1 s vs 18.1 s; 7/15 vs 6/15. A prompt chunk over a long prefix costs far more (the indexer reads the whole prefix), so the chunk shrinks as the prefix grows: 16k tokens up to a 44k prefix, 5.9k at 200k. Both GPUs of an engine finish their step together more often.

runs.name: control half at full load (adopted stack incl. cost-sized chunks)
runs.why: Control half at full load (4.42 M per GPU) on the adopted stack with cost-sized prompt chunks (pivot 44k): 9/15, generation 60.9 tok/s, median first token 1.48 s, first-token p99 12.2 s, 0 errors: the best full-load group so far.

runs.name: + smaller chunk pivot (22k instead of 44k)
runs.why: Paired against the control on the same requests: generation −2.92 tok/s (95% CI −3.8..−1.9), first token unchanged (×1.001); 6/15. Cutting long-prefix chunks harder adds generation pauses; the pivot stays at 44k and 88k is tested next.

runs.name: control half at full load (pivot 44k)
runs.why: Control half at full load (4.42 M per GPU), cost-sized chunks with pivot 44k: 7/15, generation 55.8 tok/s, median first token 1.63 s, 0 errors (re-run after the 09:12 crash; the memory park fix was in place).

runs.name: + chunk pivot 88k instead of 44k
runs.why: Paired against the control on the same requests: generation +0.98 tok/s (95% CI +0.03..+1.98), first token −5.5% (CI −8.6..−1.5%); 6/15 vs 7/15. A pivot of 44k cuts chunks too hard; 88k keeps more of the gain. 88k is now the adopted value.

runs.name: control half at full load
runs.why: Control half at full load (4.42 M per GPU): 6/15, generation 55.7 tok/s, median first token 1.53 s, 0 errors.

runs.name: + attention split across both GPUs (TP2, production's layout)
runs.why: Paired against the control on the same requests: first token ×0.53 (CI 0.51..0.55; median 0.66 s vs 1.53 s, p99 9.7 s vs 14.3 s), but generation −7.4 tok/s (CI −8.5..−6.3); 3/15. Draft acceptance is the same (3.65). Each generation step costs more: the split needs an all-reduce in every layer. The next test adds production's fused all-reduce.

runs.name: control half at full load
runs.why: Control half at full load (4.42 M per GPU): 6/15, generation 58.2 tok/s, median first token 1.52 s, 0 errors.

runs.name: + TP2 attention with fused all-reduce (production's pair)
runs.why: Paired against the control: first token ×0.53 (CI 0.50..0.56), generation −8.2 tok/s (CI −9.4..−6.7); 2/15. The fused all-reduce was active (engine log), so the all-reduce is not the main cost. Likely cause: both GPUs repeat the norm, quantization and other element-wise steps for every token. The next test keeps those activations split (--enable-attn-tp-input-scattered).

runs.name: today's replay (v3.1), adopted stack
runs.why: Control half at full load (4.42 M per GPU) on the v3.1 replay: 6/15, generation 56.2 tok/s, median first token 1.67 s, cache hit 95.1%, uncached prompt 12.9 M tokens.

runs.name: fair closed-loop replay (v3.2), same engines
runs.why: Same engines, same sessions; each follow-up carries our own earlier answers (full 1,913, partial 303; 965 with no replayed earlier turn). Paired: generation +1.53 tok/s (CI +0.2..+2.9), first token ×0.904 (CI 0.88..0.94), p99 11.8 s vs 17.7 s; uncached prompt 11.7 M (−9%), cache hit 95.5% (production 97.1%); 6/15 both. v3.2 is the test from now on.

runs.name: control half at full load
runs.why: Control half at full load (4.42 M per GPU): 7/15, generation 57.8 tok/s, median first token 1.49 s, 0 errors.

runs.name: + TP2 attention, split activations, fused all-reduce
runs.why: Paired against the control: first token ×0.58 (CI 0.55..0.61), generation −9.7 tok/s (CI −10.5..−8.4); 2/15. Splitting the activations did not help. Three TP2 variants all lose 14–17% of generation speed with our kernels; the TP2 line is closed for now.

runs.name: control half at full load (fair replay v3.2, adopted stack)
runs.why: Control half at full load (4.39 M per GPU) on the fair replay with every adopted change (cost-sized chunks, pivot 88k): 7/15, generation 61.0 tok/s, median first token 1.45 s, first-token p99 12.3 s, 0 errors; uncached prompt 11.1 M tokens.

runs.name: + longer prompt pairing (60 passes)
runs.why: Paired against the control on the same sessions: generation +0.31 tok/s (95% CI −0.6..+1.6), first token ×1.015 (CI 0.97..1.05); 7/15 both. The pairing stays at 30 passes.

runs.name: control half at full load (v3.2, adopted stack)
runs.why: Control half at full load (4.40 M per GPU) on the fair replay: 8/15, generation 59.8 tok/s, median first token 1.43 s, first-token p99 11.8 s, 0 errors.

runs.name: + DSpark draft block 6 (instead of 7)
runs.why: Paired against the control on the same sessions: generation +0.55 tok/s (95% CI −0.6..+2.1), first token ×0.979 (CI 0.95..1.01); 7/15 vs 8/15. Cheaper verify steps balance the lower acceptance. Block 7 stays.

runs.name: Full node, fair replay (v3.2), every adopted change, 1.0×
runs.why: 4.40 M per GPU, 0 errors, first token passes in every minute (1.3–2.2 s); generation passes in 3 of 15 minutes (per-minute median 53.8 tok/s; minutes 10–14 at 37–50 tok/s). Cache hit 94.9% vs production 97.1%. The twin groups (half 0 of the sessions) read 5–6 tok/s higher, so the official level comes from full-node runs.

runs.name: Full node, fair replay (v3.2), every adopted change, 0.875×
runs.why: 3.72 M per GPU, 0 errors, first token passes in every minute (1.3–1.8 s); generation 65.8 tok/s (production 64.4 on the same requests); 11 of 15 minutes pass. Minutes 10–12 and 14 fail (43–55 tok/s): bursts of 5–6 requests per minute with more than 100k uncached prompt tokens.

runs.name: control half at full load (v3.2, adopted stack with decode-after-prefill)
runs.why: Control half at full load (4.40 M per GPU): 6/15, generation 57.0 tok/s, median first token 1.41 s, 0 errors.

runs.name: − decode-after-prefill (setting off)
runs.why: Paired against the control on the same sessions: generation +2.66 tok/s (95% CI +1.6..+3.7), first token +5.8% (CI +2..+10%; median 1.44 s); 9/15 vs 6/15. With cost-sized chunks and prompt pairing in place, the forced generation step after each prompt step no longer helps. The setting is now off.

runs.name: control half at full load (v3.2)
runs.why: Control half at full load (4.41 M per GPU): 8/15, generation 60.9 tok/s, median first token 1.50 s, 0 errors.

runs.name: + long-session pool (sessions starting at 300k+ tokens on one slot)
runs.why: Paired against the control: generation −9.3 tok/s (95% CI −10.9..−7.5), first token +48%; 2/15; uncached prompt +20%. Only 2 sessions qualified (the gateway's size estimate is low), but the pool still reserved 1 of the 4 GPU slots, so normal traffic ran on 3 slots. A hard reservation wastes capacity; not retried.

runs.name: control half at full load (v3.2, adopted stack, decode-after-prefill off)
runs.why: Control half at full load (4.39 M per GPU): 10/15, generation 61.3 tok/s, median first token 1.34 s, 0 errors; uncached prompt 10.4 M tokens. This is the best control half at full load so far (decode-after-prefill is now off).

runs.name: + FA4 attention kernel for the draft model (production's draft backend)
runs.why: Paired against the control on the same sessions: generation +4.65 tok/s (95% CI +3.6..+5.9), first token ×1.005 (CI 0.96..1.03); 12/15 vs 10/15. Draft acceptance is the same (3.60). The draft now replays its CUDA graph, so its attention kernel is a real part of each generation step. On Sep 30 the same kernel gave no gain, because the draft then ran without graphs. FA4 is on in all queued runs.

runs.name: control half at full load (v3.2, adopted stack, flashinfer draft attention)
runs.why: Control half at full load (4.43 M per GPU): 10/15, generation 65.6 tok/s, median first token 1.45 s, 0 errors. The same settings gave 61.3 tok/s at 18:21: identical control halves differ by about 4 tok/s, so only paired results decide.

runs.name: smaller prompt pieces (16k per engine, 8k per GPU)
runs.why: Paired against the control on the same sessions: generation −3.24 tok/s (95% CI −4.6..−1.8), first token ×1.000; 9/15 vs 10/15. Cost-sized chunks already cap the expensive pieces; smaller pieces add more prompt steps that pause generation.

runs.name: full node, fair replay (v3.2), adopted stack with FA4 draft attention, 0.875×
runs.why: 3.72 M per GPU, 0 errors; 14 of 15 minutes pass (before FA4 and with decode-after-prefill: 11/15). Only minute 11 misses, at 59.97 tok/s. Generation 73.7 tok/s (production 64.4 on the same requests); median first token 1.2–1.7 s in every minute.

runs.name: full node, fair replay (v3.2), adopted stack with FA4 draft attention, 1.0×
runs.why: 4.41 M per GPU, 0 errors; 8 of 15 minutes pass (before FA4 and with decode-after-prefill: 3/15). Minutes 6–12 fail on generation speed (41.8–54.9 tok/s); the median first token passes in every minute (1.3–2.1 s). Generation 58.5 tok/s overall (production 64.6).

runs.name: full node, fair replay (v3.2), adopted stack with FA4 draft attention, 1.125×
runs.why: 4.99 M per GPU (sessions of buckets b00, b01 and a quarter of b02), 0 errors; 3 of 15 minutes pass. Generation 50.9 tok/s overall (production 65.1); minute 10 also misses on first token (3.91 s). The stack holds 14/15 at 3.72 M and 8/15 at 4.41 M.

runs.name: full node, fair replay (v3.2), adopted stack with FA4 draft attention, 0.75×
runs.why: 3.33 M per GPU, 0 errors; 15 of 15 minutes pass: the first pass on the fair test. Generation 81.0 tok/s (production 64.8 on the same requests); every minute 64.9–93.9 tok/s; median first token 1.2–1.6 s.

runs.name: control half at full load (v3.2, FA4 draft attention)
runs.why: Control half at full load (4.40 M per GPU): 7/15, generation 62.4 tok/s, median first token 1.34 s, 0 errors; uncached prompt 10.4 M tokens.

runs.name: + faster index-score kernel for prompt chunks (bitwise equal)
runs.why: Paired against the control on the same sessions: generation +3.62 tok/s (95% CI +2.2..+5.0), first token ×0.993 (CI 0.95..1.03); 12/15 vs 7/15. The new kernel gives the same scores bit for bit and makes long prompt chunks 4–5× faster, so prompt steps pause generation for less time. On in all queued runs.

runs.name: full node, fair replay (v3.2), FA4 draft attention, 0.875×, another node share (buckets b02+b03)
runs.why: 3.51 M per GPU on another node's sessions. Generation (62–98 tok/s) and median first token (1.2–1.5 s) pass in every minute, but 59 requests (1.1%) failed with HTTP 400, so only 1 of 15 minutes passes. All 59 come from one session: 44 of its 218 tool schemas carry "type": {}, which our engine's schema check rejects and production accepts. Gateway fix written (TOOL_SCHEMA_FIX_TYPE).

production_scoring_note: Production on the same requests, scored with the same per-minute rule from its hub logs: passes TTFT median, TTFT p99 and decode in every minute at every load; fails a minute only on the errors rule (its own 429 load-shedding and 504 timeouts). Under protocol v3.1 the 429-rejected requests are not replayed, so production's remaining errors are 504s.
simulation_note: StandardKernel inference-benchmark runs (synthetic sessions) are a cross-check only, never used to rank settings.
